messages:
Leah: customer (acme-123) opened a ticket — they got a residency alert + high latency. says requests for their EU tenant were served from us-west-2. forwarding audit id. @Maya can you look?
Maya: saw the automated alert. Compliance bot fired: residency-policy-exception for tenant acme-123. pulling logs now.
Compliance Bot: [automated] Residency policy violation detected for tenant acme-123. Fallback route used: us-west-2. Audit id: audit-20240430-7a2b. https://audit.redwood.internal/audit-20240430-7a2b
Sam: customer notes this started ~10:12 UTC after a capacity spike. latency spiked too. likely a failover.
Noah: quick check of routing config — tenant policy for acme-123 shows fallback_strategy: nearest_available which can route cross-region. that seems at odds with their residency expectation.
Raj: I see the history — ops changed fallback defaults on 2024-04-29 to allow nearest_available for some tiers. looks like residency_enforced flag existed but older router code path doesn't enforce it when pool health is low.
Maya: repro steps i used locally: 
1) curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'X-Account-Region: eu-west-1' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
2) response headers contained: X-Served-Region: us-west-2
3) correlated with audit id audit-20240430-7a2b in logs
Sam: can reproduce from my laptop too. sending screenshots in ticket.
Leah: escalate to compliance/legal — @Compliance Bot, do we need to treat this as potential cross-border data exposure?
Compliance Bot: initial triage: policy flagged. need confirmation whether payloads contained PII or customer-specified sensitive attributes. please provide redacted example payloads and timestamps.
Noah: I'm preparing a hotfix to ensure residency_enforced is honored in the router selection path. patching now, will restart eu router pool after test. ETA ~22m.
Raj: mitigation in place — changed tenant fallback to regional-only for acme-123: 
```
UPDATE tenant_policies SET fallback_strategy='regional-only' WHERE tenant_id='acme-123';
```
Maya: applied the change and running smoke tests against sample traffic.
Maya: smoke looks good. sample requests now show X-Served-Region: eu-west-1.
Leah: note for CS/billing — customer might have seen extra cost/latency due to cross-region serving. @Sam please draft a customer-friendly summary with timeline and remediation steps, include audit id.
Sam: on it. will loop in legal & compliance for wording.
Ops Oncall: created incident INC-20240430-4321 and invited SRE. tagging for postmortem.
Noah: pushed PR for router fix: https://github.com/redwood/route/commit/abcd123 — includes unit tests for residency enforcement. will roll to canary once smoke passes.
Leah: thanks — keep this thread updated with audit dump and PR status. we need the full audit export for compliance. :thumbsup:
